scope: 逐项翻译冻结的独立英文读回；论文来源材料另存，不进入形式读回。
guidelines: docs/三语自然语言读回原则.md
docs/三语术语名词关键对照.md

zh_Hans.basis: 沿用现有读回中最小多项式、自然数次数、Möbius 映射、初等映射、分歧指数、根重数、有理数代数嵌入等用语；人名 Möbius 保留原拼写。

ja.basis: 沿用既有读回中的メビウス変換、初等写像、分岐指数、最小多項式、根の重複度等领域用语；未声称逐页核对日语参考。

readbacks.en: For every element $x$ of the specified algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ of $\mathbb Q$, if the natural-number degree of its minimal polynomial over $\mathbb Q$ is at most $1$, then there exists a rational number $q$ such that $x$ equals the image of $q$ under the canonical embedding $\mathbb Q\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathbb Q}$. The degree bound is inclusive; although it syntactically permits degree $0$, every element of this algebraic closure has a minimal polynomial of positive degree. The declaration has no variable universe, arbitrary field, or additional typeclass hypothesis.
readbacks.zh_Hans: 对指定的有理数域 $\mathbb Q$ 的代数闭包 $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ 中的每个元素 $x$，若 $x$ 在 $\mathbb Q$ 上的最小多项式的自然数次数至多为 $1$，则存在有理数 $q$，使 $x$ 等于 $q$ 在标准嵌入 $\mathbb Q\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathbb Q}$ 下的像。次数上界包含等号；虽然该条件在语法上允许次数为 $0$，但此代数闭包中每个元素的最小多项式的次数都为正。该声明没有可变的宇宙参数、任意域参数或额外的类型类假设。
readbacks.ja: 指定された有理数体 $\mathbb Q$ の代数閉包 $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ の任意の元 $x$ に対し、$x$ の $\mathbb Q$ 上の最小多項式の自然数次数が $1$ 以下ならば、有理数 $q$ が存在し、$x$ は標準埋め込み $\mathbb Q\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathbb Q}$ による $q$ の像に等しい。次数の上限は等号を含む。この条件は構文上は次数 $0$ を許すが、この代数閉包の各元の最小多項式の次数は正である。この宣言には可変の宇宙パラメータ、任意の体のパラメータ、追加の型クラスの仮定はない。

readbacks.en:
For every finite set $T\subseteq\mathbb Q$ and every rational number $	au$, if $|t|\le1$ for every $t\in T$ and $9\le	au$, then there exists a finite list of allowed elementary maps such that its associated $F$ and $E$ satisfy all three conditions: $F(z)\in\{\infty,0,1\}$ for every $z$ in $\{\infty\}\cup\{t:t\in T\}$, with rational elements regarded as their canonical images in $\overline{\mathbb Q}$; $F(	au)
otin\{\infty,0,1\}$; and, for every $z\in P$, the strict inequality $1<E(z)$ implies $F(z)\in\{\infty,0,1\}$. Here $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ is the specified algebraic closure of $\mathbb Q$, and $P=\overline{\mathbb Q}\cup\{\infty\}$ is represented by adjoining one distinct point $\infty$. An allowed elementary map is either a Möbius map $m(z)=(az+b)/(cz+d)$ with $a,b,c,d\in\mathbb Q$ and $ad-bc
e0$, or a polynomial $p\in\mathbb Q[X]$ whose natural-number degree is strictly positive. A Möbius map sends a finite $z$ to $\infty$ when $cz+d=0$, otherwise to the displayed quotient; at $\infty$ its value is $\infty$ if $c=0$, and the rational number $a/c$ embedded in $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ if $c
e0$. A polynomial sends finite $z$ to $p(z)$ and sends $\infty$ to $\infty$. The elementary ramification number $e_m(z)$ is $1$ everywhere for a Möbius map; for a polynomial $p$ it is $\deg p$ at $\infty$ and the multiplicity of $z$ as a root of $\overline p(X)-\overline p(z)$ at finite $z$, where $\overline p$ is obtained by embedding the rational coefficients into $\overline{\mathbb Q}$. For a list $h_1,\ldots,h_n$, put $z_0=z$, $z_i=h_i(z_{i-1})$, $F(z)=z_n$, and $E(z)=\prod_{i=1}^n e_{h_i}(z_{i-1})$; the empty list is permitted and gives $F(z)=z$ and $E(z)=1$. The finite set $T$ may be empty, but the required source set still contains $\infty$; the bounds $|t|\le1$ and $9\le	au$ include their endpoints. The declaration has no variable universe, arbitrary field, or additional typeclass hypothesis.

Here $\iota:\overline{\mathbb Q}\hookrightarrow\mathbb C$ is the particular rational-algebra embedding fixed by the supplied definition using an algebraically closed field lift, and $\|\cdot\|$ is the usual complex norm; the hypothesis concerns this chosen embedding. Here $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ is the specified algebraic closure of $\mathbb Q$, and $P=\overline{\mathbb Q}\cup\{\infty\}$ is represented by adjoining one distinct point $\infty$. An allowed elementary map is either a Möbius map $m(z)=(az+b)/(cz+d)$ with $a,b,c,d\in\mathbb Q$ and $ad-bc
e0$, or a polynomial $p\in\mathbb Q[X]$ whose natural-number degree is strictly positive. e0$. A polynomial sends finite $z$ to $p(z)$ and sends $\infty$ to $\infty$. The finite set $T$ may be empty, but the required source set still contains $\infty$; both numerical upper bounds are inclusive, and although the degree bound syntactically permits degree $0$, every element of $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ has a minimal polynomial of positive degree.
